https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-release/release.md#issuepr-kind-label

4. If you want *faster* PR reviews, read how: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#best-practices-for-faster-reviews
5. If the PR is unfinished, see how to mark it: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#marking-unfinished-pull-requests
-->

#### What type of PR is this?

<!--
Add one of the following kinds:
/kind bug
/kind cleanup
/kind documentation
/kind feature

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change
/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test
/kind flake
/kind regression
-->
/kind feature
/kind api-change

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
PodTopologySpread is widely used in production environments, especially in service type workloads which employ Deployments. However, currently it has a limitation that manifests during rolling updates which causes the deployment to end up out of balance ([98215](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/98215), [105661](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/105661),[k8s-pod-topology spread is not respected after rollout](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/66510883/k8s-pod-topology-spread-is-not-respected-after-rollout)). 

The root cause is that PodTopologySpread constraints allow defining a key-value label selector, which applies to all pods in a Deployment irrespective of their owning ReplicaSet. As a result, when a new revision is rolled out, spreading will apply across pods from both the old and new ReplicaSets, and so by the time the new ReplicaSet is completely rolled out and the old one is rolled back, the actual spreading we are left with may not match expectations because the deleted pods from the older ReplicaSet will cause skewed distribution for the remaining pods.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes #98215
Fixes #105661

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
<!--
If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.
If yes, a release note is required:
Enter your extended release note in the block below. If the PR requires additional action from users switching to the new release, include the string "action required".

For more information on release notes see: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/release-notes.md
-->
```release-note
Respect PodTopologySpread after rolling upgrades
```

#### Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.:

<!--
This section can be blank if this pull request does not require a release note.

When adding links which point to resources within git repositories, like
KEPs or supporting documentation, please reference a specific commit and avoid
linking directly to the master branch. This ensures that links reference a
specific point in time, rather than a document that may change over time.

See here for guidance on getting permanent links to files: https://help.github.com/en/articles/getting-permanent-links-to-files

Please use the following format for linking documentation:
- [KEP]: <link>
- [Usage]: <link>
- [Other doc]: <link>
-->
- [KEP]: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3243)

issue_context.title: Rolling updates interfere with Pod Topology Spread Constraints
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->

**Background**:
We define Pod Topology Spread Constraints on our Deployment (labeled `app: app1`), as follows:
>       topologySpreadConstraints:
>       - maxSkew: 1
>         topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
>         whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
>         labelSelector:
>           matchLabels:
>             app: app1

The deployment is defined with 5 replicas.

**What happened**:
Triggering a rolling update on the running deployment will sometimes result in a skewed spread, not honoring the maxSkew=1.
Our theory is that the scheduler "sees" the old pods when deciding how to spread the new pods over nodes. When the old nodes are eventually terminated, we sometimes see three pods in node-1, two pods in node-2 and none in node-3.

**What you expected to happen**:
The maxSkew value in Pod Topology Spread Constraints should always be honored.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
It reproduces randomly, so it takes a few attempts until reproduced.
I'm running `kubectl rollout restart deployment <deployment-name>` a few times until it reproduces.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.19.7
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: self deployed cluster with kubeadm on on-premises VMs (vmware)
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): CentOS 7
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 3.10.0-1160.6.1.el7.x86_64
- Other: cluster consists of 3 master nodes which also act as workers

from source code comments, `A constraint is considered "Unsatisfiable" for an incoming pod if and only if every possible node assigment for that pod would violate "MaxSkew" on some topology.` @roizentner , in your case, node-1(3) - node-2(2) = 1 don't violate this rule
i think ,   node-1(3)/node-2(2)/node-3(0) just one of satisfiable cases , node-1(3)/node-2(1)/node-3(1) also satisfiable

@roizentner This case may possibly happen and is actually a general scale-down / rolling update problem - choosing which replicas to delete is controlled by controller-manager instead of scheduler, so controller manager may not have the context to choose the most optimal replicas to remove.

Back to this issue, in particular 5-replicas on 3 nodes, the chances to result in a violated distribution should be very rare. I tried ~10 times in latest code, but no luck to reproduce.

1. Could you paste the output of `k get pod -o wide -w` when you're able to reproduce? (start the command before performing rolling update, and stop until the update is complete)
2. Also, I'm suspicious you have a non-default setting on `maxSurge` or(and) `maxUnavailable`. If so, could you change it to the following settings and retry?
    ```yaml
    strategy:
      rollingUpdate:
        maxSurge: 1
        maxUnavailable: 1
      type: RollingUpdate
    ```

One hack to avoid this race condition between the old and new ReplicaSet is to update the topology-spread selector with each deployment update:

The pod template could look like the following, with each update to the deployment, change the version:

```
metadata:                                                                                                                                                                                                     
    labels:                                                                                                                                                                                                     
      app: app1
      version: v1                                                                                                                                                                                             
  spec:                       
    topologySpreadConstraints:
      - maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
        whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
        labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: app1
            version: v1
```

> I mean, if I run `kubectl scale` or `kubectl set image` for example, that would trigger a rolling update so I would need to set the selector's new value simultaneously somehow. Is there a way to do that?

You can pause the deployment using `kubectl rollout pause deployment.v1.apps/<deployment-name>`, then 
make the changes you want, like setting a new scale, image or updating pod labels and pod-topology selectors, then resume: `kubectl rollout resume deployment.v1.apps/<deployment-name>`

At certain moment in time the skew will be proper.
But when the pods that are to be removed will be removed the skew might be skewed :)
Essentially you are facing the limitation described here:

[Scaling down a Deployment may result in imbalanced Pods distribution.](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-topology-spread-constraints/)
One simple workaround I apply is **scale it down + restart/deploy + scale it up.**

Then the skew is perfectly fine!

The following might be of interest to those in this thread.

Kubernetes v1.20.11
Ubuntu 16.04.1
TKGi vSphere NSX-T

My cluster and topology looks like:
```
master/449d1d0f-8e51-49d0-8759-41dcd8d64450:~$ k get nodes -o wide --show-labels | grep  windows | awk -F' |=' '{print $1 " " $17 " " $48}'
3ebcdcd1-d647-4814-a14d-66ca3bd85313 172.42.129.8 az2
41300042-c376-42e9-b7bb-d40f2330f18e 172.42.129.7 az2
92db06e7-1258-417f-9bd7-e8644059aa7b 172.42.129.6 az1
9cd0d589-f959-4117-8c01-a1b0eb5d931e 172.42.129.9 az3
```

But when using a rolling deployment, the new pods can end up in imbalanced topologies that violate the specified maxSkew. This is due to interference from the old Terminating pods in the scheduler's topology size calculation. At scheduling time, the constraints are technically satisfied, however, once the old pods are removed, the topology size difference can be greater than maxSkew.

For example:
```
master/449d1d0f-8e51-49d0-8759-41dcd8d64450:~$ cat /tmp/az-spread-test.yaml 
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: az-spread-test
  name: az-spread-test
spec:
  replicas: 21
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: az-spread-test
  template:
    metadata:
      creationTimestamp: null
      labels:
        app: az-spread-test
    spec:
      affinity:
        nodeAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            nodeSelectorTerms:
            - matchExpressions:
              - key: os
                operator: In
                values:
                - windows
      containers:
      - image: nginx
        name: nginx
      topologySpreadConstraints:
      - labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: az-spread-test
        maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
```

Created deployment:
```
master/449d1d0f-8e51-49d0-8759-41dcd8d64450:~$ k apply -f /tmp/az-spread-test.yaml 
deployment.apps/az-spread-test created
```

Confirmed that pods are balanced across AZs:
```
master/449d1d0f-8e51-49d0-8759-41dcd8d64450:~$ for node in $(kubectl get po -o wide | grep -v NODE | awk '{print $7}'); do k get node $node --show-labels | grep -v NAME | cut -d'=' -f14; done | sort | uniq -c
      7 az1
      7 az2
      7 az3
```

Performed a rolling update and reproduced the imbalanced topology that I've described above:
```
master/449d1d0f-8e51-49d0-8759-41dcd8d64450:~$ kubectl set image deployment/az-spread-test nginx=nginx:1.17 --record
deployment.apps/az-spread-test image updated

master/449d1d0f-8e51-49d0-8759-41dcd8d64450:~$ kubectl rollout status deployment/az-spread-test
Waiting for deployment "az-spread-test" rollout to finish: 20 of 21 updated replicas are available...
deployment "az-spread-test" successfully rolled out

master/449d1d0f-8e51-49d0-8759-41dcd8d64450:~$ for node in $(kubectl get po -o wide | grep -v NODE | awk '{print $7}'); do k get node $node --show-labels | grep -v NAME | cut -d'=' -f14; done | sort | uniq -c
      8 az1
      4 az2
      9 az3
```

I got around the imbalance issue during rolling updates and scaling down. The update has to be done by modifying the deployment yaml and adding and incrementing a version label for each apply.

For example:
```
master/449d1d0f-8e51-49d0-8759-41dcd8d64450:~$ cat /tmp/az-spread-test.yaml 
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: az-spread-test
  name: az-spread-test
spec:
  replicas: 21
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: az-spread-test
  template:
    metadata:
      creationTimestamp: null
      labels:
        app: az-spread-test
        version: v1
    spec:
      affinity:
        nodeAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            nodeSelectorTerms:
            - matchExpressions:
              - key: os
                operator: In
                values:
                - windows
      containers:
      - image: nginx
        name: nginx
      topologySpreadConstraints:
      - labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: az-spread-test
            version: v1
        maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
```

Created deployment with image nginx and 21 replicas:
```
master/449d1d0f-8e51-49d0-8759-41dcd8d64450:~$ k apply -f /tmp/az-spread-test.yaml --record
deployment.apps/az-spread-test created
```

Pods balanced across the AZs:
```
master/449d1d0f-8e51-49d0-8759-41dcd8d64450:~$ for node in $(kubectl get po -o wide | grep -v NODE | awk '{print $7}'); do k get node $node --show-labels | grep -v NAME | cut -d'=' -f14; done | sort | uniq -c
      7 az1
      7 az2
      7 az3
```

Incremented the version to v2, changed the image to nginx:1.17 and changed the replicas to 15:
```
master/449d1d0f-8e51-49d0-8759-41dcd8d64450:~$ cat /tmp/az-spread-test.yaml 
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: az-spread-test
  name: az-spread-test
spec:
  replicas: 15
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: az-spread-test
  template:
    metadata:
      creationTimestamp: null
      labels:
        app: az-spread-test
        version: v2
    spec:
      affinity:
        nodeAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            nodeSelectorTerms:
            - matchExpressions:
              - key: os
                operator: In
                values:
                - windows
      containers:
      - image: nginx:1.17
        name: nginx
      topologySpreadConstraints:
      - labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: az-spread-test
            version: v2
        maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
```

New deployment rolled out with new image, scaled down and still balanced across AZs:
```
master/449d1d0f-8e51-49d0-8759-41dcd8d64450:~$ k apply -f /tmp/az-spread-test.yaml --record
deployment.apps/az-spread-test configured

master/449d1d0f-8e51-49d0-8759-41dcd8d64450:~$ for node in $(kubectl get po -o wide | grep -v NODE | awk '{print $7}'); do k get node $node --show-labels | grep -v NAME | cut -d'=' -f14; done | sort | uniq -c
      5 az1
      5 az2
      5 az3
```

This field needs to be validated:
1) validate that the keys are valid keys, I think you can use [ValidateLabelName]( https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e092b6d27bff004171b71fffa45f111fdcd6e81b/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/validation/validation.go#L62), and we should call it from [validateTopologySpreadConstraints](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9f9602ef830d55e844ad500c0a3ab342dd7cc98d/pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go#L6468)
2) validate that it is neither set nor updated when the feature flag is disabled, similar to [dropDisabledNodeInclusionPolicyFields](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9f9602ef830d55e844ad500c0a3ab342dd7cc98d/pkg/api/pod/util.go#L555)
Done
We probably better validate that a key in matchLabelKeys don't exist in labelSelector. It doesn't seem like there is a use case for it, so better block it.

I feel that this is too strict and lacks flexibility. Maybe like labelSelector, it will also may be contradicted with the use of the same key in both labelSelector and matchExpressions. But we don't block it? right? 
```go
kind: Pod
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: mypod
  labels:
    foo: a  
spec:
  topologySpreadConstraints:
  - maxSkew: 1
    topologyKey: zone
    whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
    labelSelector:
      matchLabels: ---> foo = a
        foo: a
      matchExpressions:   --> foo in {b}
      - key: foo
        operator: In
        values:
        - b
  containers:
  - name: pause
    image: k8s.gcr.io/pause:3.1
```
The keys in matchLabelKeys and labelSelector do not necessarily contradict each other. Maybe just some cases.
But lacks flexibility to do what? What is the use case? The example you gave above translates to a selector that matches nothing, which probably isn't what the user intended to do.

Yes. You are right. This case is not the user intend to do. 
I added the validation for this.
